Class ReflectionAnnotations

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.reflection.ReflectionAnnotations
public final class ReflectionAnnotations extends Object
Builds AnnotationMetadata and AnnotationValues from the annotations read reflectively from an AnnotatedElement, in the shape the annotation processors give the metadata they generate at compilation time.

Code written against generated metadata then works unchanged for an element that has none:

  • the meta-annotations of an annotation are its stereotypes, recursively, with their values;
  • a repeatable annotation is filed under its container, whether it was written once, several times or inside the container, and the container is registered so that AnnotationMetadata.getAnnotationValuesByType(Class) finds it;
  • the defaults of the members are registered and reachable through AnnotationMetadata.getDefaultValues(String) and the value accessors;
  • a class value is an AnnotationClassValue, an enum value is its name, a nested annotation is an AnnotationValue;
  • the members annotated NonBinding are recorded, so that a qualifier built from the metadata ignores them;
  • an annotation a class inherits through Inherited is present but not declared, from a super class as from an interface of its hierarchy, which the processors walk and Class.getAnnotations() leaves out.

An annotation instance does not say which members were written, so a member whose value equals its default is not part of the values of the annotation; it is served by the defaults, as a member that was not written is at compilation time.

The annotation mappers, transformers and remappers of the annotation processors are not applied: they are part of micronaut-core-processor and are not on a runtime classpath. The ReflectionAnnotationCustomizer services are their runtime counterpart, and receive the values of every annotation this class converts.

Since:
5.2.0
Author:
Denis Stepanov

    • declaring

      public static AnnotationMetadata declaring(Class<? extends Annotation> annotationType, Map<CharSequence, Object> values)
      The metadata of an element that declares an annotation type, without an instance of it: the annotation with the values given, its defaults and its stereotypes, as the processors record it.

      Code that adapts another container - a Guice binding annotation, a Spring bean marked primary - knows the annotation type and the members it means, and has no instance to read. Declaring the annotation by name alone loses its defaults and its stereotypes, and a qualifier built from such metadata then fails to match one built from the generated metadata of a bean.

      Parameters:
      annotationType - The annotation type, filed under its container when it is repeatable
      values - The values of the members, empty when the annotation is written bare
      Returns:
      The metadata

    • merge

      public static AnnotationMetadata merge(AnnotationMetadata first, AnnotationMetadata second)
      The annotations of two metadata in one, both declared: the metadata of a class together with the annotations another container means it to carry.

      A container adapting another one - a Spring bean it marks primary, a Guice binding it qualifies - has annotations of its own to add to the ones a class declares. Replacing the metadata of the class loses what the class says; a hierarchy keeps both but only the last level counts as declared, and the framework reads a scope, a qualifier and a primary marker from the declared level. This merges them, so both are declared.

      Parameters:
      first - The metadata whose values win where both declare the same annotation
      second - The metadata to add
      Returns:
      The merged metadata

    • values

      public static Map<CharSequence, Object> values(Annotation annotation)
      The values of the members of an annotation, as the metadata stores them: the members whose value is the default of the member are left out, a class is an AnnotationClassValue, an enum constant is its name, a nested annotation is an AnnotationValue and the members annotated NonBinding are listed under AnnotationUtil.NON_BINDING_ATTRIBUTE.

      A nested annotation is given the same treatment as the annotation holding it, recursively, and an array value is a copy the caller owns.

      Parameters:
      annotation - The annotation
      Returns:
      The values, mutable
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - When a member of the annotation cannot be read
